exporting triage decisions. Follows inbox.ts command registration pattern.


Acceptance Criteria (17):
  [ac-1]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <inbox-ref> --action promote --reasoning "clear feature request"

    When: the inbox item exists

    Then: creates a TriageRecord with item_snapshot from inbox item,
status triaged, the given action and reasoning, and commits
to shadow branch

  [ac-2]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list

    When: triage records exist

    Then: displays records with ULID prefix, item snapshot (truncated),
status, action, decided_by, and relative time

  [ac-3]
    Given: user runs kspec triage list --status pending

    When: records with various statuses exist

    Then: only records matching the status filter are shown

  [ac-4]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status triaged and action promote

    Then: executes the promote action (creates task from snapshot),
transitions record to acted_on with acted_at and result_ref

  [ac-5]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action delete

    When: the referenced inbox item still exists

    Then: deletes the inbox item without additional confirmation (the
triage decision serves as prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-6]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action defer

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: transitions to acted_on with no side effect beyond recording the deferral

  [ac-7]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action spec-gap

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: creates an observation tagged spec-gap with the item snapshot
and reasoning, transitions record to acted_on with result_ref

  [ac-8]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> on a record with action duplicate

    When: the record is triaged

    Then: deletes the inbox item (prior authorization) and transitions
record to acted_on

  [ac-9]
    Given: user runs kspec triage start

    When: untriaged inbox items exist

    Then: enters interactive mode presenting items one at a time,
prompting for action and reasoning, creating triage records
for each, skipping already-triaged items

  [ac-10]
    Given: the user aborts interactive triage mode with Ctrl+C

    When: some items have been triaged

    Then: all previously committed triage records are preserved

  [ac-11]
    Given: user runs kspec triage record <ref> with --json flag

    When: the command succeeds

    Then: outputs the created triage record as structured JSON

  [ac-12]
    Given: user runs kspec triage override <triage-ref> --action defer --reasoning "not ready yet"

    When: the triage record exists with an existing decision

    Then: updates the record with override_reasoning, override_by,
override_at, and the new action

  [ac-13]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format context

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a markdown context block per record with item text,
action, reasoning, decided_by, evidence refs, and outcome

  [ac-14]
    Given: user runs kspec triage export --format json

    When: triage records exist

    Then: outputs a JSON array with full TriageRecord objects

  [ac-15]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status acted_on (already executed)

    Then: returns an error with guidance that the record has already been acted on

  [ac-16]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref>

    When: the record has status pending (no decision yet)

    Then: returns an error with guidance to record a decision first

  [ac-17]
    Given: user runs kspec triage act <triage-ref> with --dry-run flag

    When: the record has status triaged

    Then: shows what action would be taken without executing it

# PR #474 Review

## Findings

1. SHOULD-FIX — "'`src/triage/actions.ts:49`

Shared `executeTriageAction()` now returns `{}` when `record.action` is missing. In the CLI flow (`triage act`), the caller unconditionally transitions the record to `acted_on` after execution. # PR #474 Review

## Findings

1. SHOULD-FIX — `src/triage/actions.ts:49`

Shared `executeTriageAction()` now returns `{}` when `record.action` is missing. In the CLI flow (`triage act`), the caller unconditionally transitions the record to `acted_on` after execution. Before this refactor, the CLI-local executor exited with a validation error (`Record has no action to execute`) instead of silently no-oping.

Impact: malformed or legacy triage records with `status=triaged` but no `action` can now be incorrectly marked as acted on.

Suggested fix: preserve the CLI behavior by either:
- throwing/returning an error from `executeTriageAction()` when `action` is absent (and letting daemon explicitly opt into silent behavior if desired), or
- adding a CLI-side guard before calling `executeTriageAction()` / before transitioning state.

## AC / Trait Coverage Check

- Task trailer found: `Task: @task-extract-triage-action-executor`
- Linked spec: `@triage-cli-commands`
- Inherited traits inspected via `kspec item get @triage-cli-commands`
- Existing `tests/triage-cli.test.ts` already contains broad `// AC:` annotations for spec ACs and inherited traits.
- New `tests/triage-actions.test.ts` adds execution-path regression coverage for `@triage-cli-commands` ac-4..8, ac-17.
- No new PR-specific AC annotation gap identified.

## Validation / Test Results

- `pnpm vitest run tests/triage-actions.test.ts` ✅
- `pnpm vitest run tests/daemon-api-triage.test.ts` ✅
- `npm run typecheck -- --pretty false` ✅
- `kspec validate` ❌ (repo-wide existing failures: reference ambiguity, alignment warnings, completeness warnings incl. trait coverage warnings not attributable to this PR)

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

	ItemSummary,
	ItemDetail,
	InboxItem,
	SessionContext,
	Observation,
	PaginatedResponse,
	SearchResponse,
	SearchResult
} from '@kynetic-ai/shared';
import type { KspecSnapshot, ExportedTask, ExportedItem } from '$lib/types/snapshot';
import { getSnapshot, ReadOnlyModeError } from '$lib/stores/mode.svelte';

/**
 * Convert ExportedTask to TaskSummary
 */

	return {
		_ulid: task._ulid,
		slugs: task.slugs,
		title: task.title,
		type: task.type,
		status: task.status,
		priority: task.priority,
		spec_ref: task.spec_ref ?? undefined,
		tags: task.tags,
		depends_on: task.depends_on,

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

_ulid: 01KEZCJPHVBKRZQ7VVBF84H51Z
slugs:
  - cli
  - cli-module
title: CLI Interface
type: module
status:
  maturity: draft
  implementation: implemented
description: |
  The kspec CLI is the primary interface to Kynetic Spec.
  Follows git's plumbing/porcelain model: low-level primitives
  for scripts/agents, high-level commands for humans.
features:
  - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHW3CSMXYZT01FP76BM
    slugs:
      - cli-design
    title: CLI Design Principles
    type: feature
    status:
      maturity: draft
      implementation: implemented
    priority: high
    tags:
      - mvp
      - cli
    description: |
      The CLI is designed for both human and agent use.
      Consistent structure, predictable output, clear errors.
    requirements:
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWP32HK8MR38P2WSSJ
        slugs:
          - cli-structure
        title: Command Structure
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          Commands follow consistent structure:

          kspec <resource> <action> [args] [flags]

          Resources: item, task, link, todo, etc.
          Actions: add, get, list, set, delete, etc.

          Examples:
          - kspec item add --type feature --title "Login"
          - kspec task start @impl-login
          - kspec tasks ready
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWKVBFSAEP0MMH57DQ
        slugs:
          - cli-json-output
        title: JSON Output Mode
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          All commands support --json flag for structured output:

          kspec tasks ready --json
          kspec item get @login --json

          JSON output includes:
          - success: boolean
          - data: The result
          - errors: Array of error objects (if any)
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWB81SAWT4ZGCV75FC
        slugs:
          - cli-exit-codes
        title: Semantic Exit Codes
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
        description: |
          Exit codes are semantic, not just 0/1:

          - 0: Success
          - 1: General error
          - 2: Usage error (bad arguments)
          - 3: Not found
          - 4: Validation failed
          - 5: Conflict (already exists, etc.)

          Scripts can handle specific cases.
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: exit-code-constants
            given: CLI codebase uses exit codes
            when: Commands need to exit with specific code
            then: Uses named constants from a centralized EXIT_CODES object (e.g., EXIT_CODES.NOT_FOUND instead
              of magic number 3)
          - id: exit-codes-documented
            given: User wants to script kspec commands
            when: User runs kspec help --exit-codes or checks documentation
            then: All exit codes are listed with their meanings and which commands may return them
          - id: consistent-usage
            given: Multiple commands use exit codes
            when: Commands exit with errors
            then: All commands use consistent exit codes for the same error types (e.g., all 'not found' errors
              exit 3, all validation errors exit 4)
        notes:
          - _ulid: 01KFADD1NW999DBZJHBDBSPFZM
            created_at: 2026-01-19T05:59:47.645Z
            author: "@claude"
            content: >-
              Enhancement: Formalize exit code implementation


              **Current state:** Exit codes are defined in spec but implementation uses magic
              numbers inconsistently.


              **Goals:**

              1. Centralized constants - single source of truth

              2. Documentation - help users script with kspec

              3. Consistency audit - ensure all commands follow the spec


              **Exit code definitions (from spec):**

              - 0: SUCCESS - Operation completed successfully

              - 1: ERROR - General/unexpected error

              - 2: USAGE - Bad arguments, invalid command usage

              - 3: NOT_FOUND - Referenced item doesn't exist

              - 4: VALIDATION - Spec validation failed

              - 5: CONFLICT - Item already exists, duplicate slug, etc.


              **New additions to consider:**

              - 6: PARTIAL - Some operations succeeded, some failed (for batch operations)


              **Documentation format:** Add to 'kspec help' or new 'kspec help --exit-codes'
              subcommand showing all codes with descriptions.
            supersedes: null
      - _ulid: 01KEZCJPHWBEEP2BYRP6YVNK9F
        slugs:
          - cli-agent-features
        title: Agent-Friendly Features
        type: requirement
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: verified
        description: |
          Features for agent/script usage:

          - --json: Structured output
          - --no-prompt: Never prompt (KSPEC_NO_PROMPT=1)
          - --dry-run: Show what would happen
          - --if-not-exists: Idempotent creation
          - --quiet: Suppress non-essential output

          Agents should be able to use kspec without interaction.
        implements:
          - "@cli-design"
        requirements:
          - _ulid: 01KHA83NH88Q21QF947XXRDRBE
            slugs:
              - output-format-option
            title: Output Format Option
            type: requirement
            tags: []
            description: |
              Add a --format <json|yaml> global option with --json, --raw, and --yaml as
              shorthands. Agents frequently try --raw and --yaml flags expecting structured
              output. --raw is a shorthand for --format json (agents associate raw with
              give me the data). --yaml is a shorthand for --format yaml. --json remains
              as a shorthand for --format json. The --format option is extensible for
              future formats. This replaces the precedence model in @trait-json-output
              ac-6 with explicit format selection.
            acceptance_criteria:
              - id: ac-format-json
                given: User runs any command with --format json
                when: The format option is set to json
                then: Output is identical to current --json behavior
              - id: ac-format-yaml
                given: User runs any command with --format yaml
                when: The format option is set to yaml
                then: Output contains the same data as --json but serialized as valid YAML
              - id: ac-json-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --json
                when: The --json shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format json (backward compatible, existing behavior preserved)
              - id: ac-raw-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --raw
                when: The --raw shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format json (same data, JSON serialization)
              - id: ac-yaml-shorthand
                given: User runs any command with --yaml
                when: The --yaml shorthand is used
                then: Equivalent to --format yaml
              - id: ac-conflict-error
                given: User runs a command with conflicting format options (e.g. --json --yaml)
                when: Multiple format specifications are provided
                then: Error message explains the conflict and exits non-zero
              - id: ac-yaml-no-ansi
                given: User runs any command with --format yaml
                when: YAML output is generated
                then: Output contains no ANSI escape codes (same contract as --json)
              - id: ac-yaml-references
                given: User runs kspec task get @ref --yaml
                when: Output contains reference fields
                then: References include @ prefix (same contract as --json)
              - id: ac-global-scope
                given: User runs any command that supports structured output with --format, --yaml, or --raw
                when: The option is used on any command
                then: The option works globally (same scope as --json)
              - id: ac-unsupported-format
                given: User runs --format csv or another unsupported format name
                when: An invalid format value is provided
                then: Error message lists valid formats (json, yaml) and exits non-zero
            depends_on: []
            implements: []
            relates_to: []
            tests: []
            traits:
              - "@trait-json-output"
              - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
            notes: []
            created: 2026-02-13T00:58:41.064Z
            status:
              maturity: draft
              implementation: implemented
      - _ulid: 01KFHZSJVGEX3KTM5CHM8J1XAN
        slugs:
          - cli-version
        title: CLI Version Display
        type: requirement
        tags: []
        description: The CLI must display the correct version from package.json when running 'kspec
          --version' or 'kspec -V'. Version must stay in sync with the npm package version.
        depends_on: []
        implements: []
        relates_to: []
        tests: []
        traits: []
        notes: []
        created: 2026-01-22T04:35:53.841Z
        acceptance_criteria:
          - id: ac-1
            given: kspec is installed from npm
            when: user runs 'kspec --version' or 'kspec -V'
            then: displays the version from package.json (e.g., '0.1.1')
          - id: ac-2
            given: a new version is released
            when: package.json version is updated
            then: CLI --version output automatically reflects the new version without code changes
          - id: ac-3
            given: kspec is run in development via 'npm run dev'
            when: user runs 'npm run dev -- --version'
            then: displays the same version as package.json
        status:
          maturity: draft
          implementation: implemented
    features:
      - _ulid: 01KGR05MC5ZTSVV9MEFF1A3AN3
        slugs:
          - batch-exec
        title: Batch Command Execution
        type: feature
        tags: []
        depends_on: []
        implements: []
        relates_to: []
        tests: []
        traits:
          - "@trait-json-output"
          - "@trait-semantic-exit-codes"
          - "@trait-error-guidance"
          - "@trait-dry-run"
          - "@trait-shadow-commit"
        notes: []
        created: 2026-02-05T22:53:37.029Z
        requirements:
          - _ulid: 01KGR05MEAH53X163Q1FAW8Y9Z
            slugs:
              - batch-command-schema
            title: Batch Command Schema
            type: requirement
            tags: []
            depends_on: []
            implements: []
            relates_to: []

    slugs:

    title: JSON Output Mode
    type: trait
    description: Commands support --json flag for structured JSON output with consistent formatting
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: command supports JSON mode
        when: --json flag is provided
        then: output is valid JSON with no ANSI color codes
      - id: ac-2
        given: JSON mode is active
        when: command completes successfully
        then: output includes all data available in human-readable mode
      - id: ac-3
        given: JSON mode is active
        when: command encounters an error
        then: error is returned as JSON object with error field
      - id: ac-4
        given: JSON output contains references
        when: output is generated
        then: references use @ prefix consistently
      - id: ac-5
        given: JSON output contains timestamps
        when: output is generated
        then: timestamps use ISO 8601 format
      - id: ac-6
        given: command supports --json
        when: used with other formatting flags
        then: --json takes precedence over other format options
  - _ulid: 01KFDZSHFAV02EW1F6Y20MAF51
    slugs:
      - trait-multi-ref-batch
    title: Multi-Reference Batch Operations
    type: trait
    description: Commands support --refs flag to operate on multiple items in a single invocation
    acceptance_criteria:
      - id: ac-1
        given: command supports batch mode
        when: --refs @ref1 @ref2 @ref3 is provided
        then: command operates on all provided references
      - id: ac-2
        given: batch operation encounters errors
        when: processing multiple refs
        then: continue processing remaining refs and report all failures
      - id: ac-3
        given: batch operation is running
        when: all refs succeed
        then: exit code 0 is returned
      - id: ac-4
        given: batch operation is running
        when: any refs fail
        then: exit code 1 is returned
      - id: ac-5
        given: batch operation output
        when: operation completes
        then: success and failure counts are reported
      - id: ac-6
        given: --refs is provided
        when: used with positional ref argument
        then: error indicating mutually exclusive options
      - id: ac-7
        given: batch operation in JSON mode
        when: --json --refs @a @b provided
        then: output array contains result for each ref
      - id: ac-8
        given: batch operation with duplicate refs
        when: --refs @a @a @b provided
        then: each ref processed once only
    status:
      maturity: draft
      implementation: implemented

    slugs:

    title: Confirmation Prompt for Destructive Operations
    type: trait

      - id: ac-1
        given: command is destructive
        when: executed without --force
        then: prompt for user confirmation before proceeding
      - id: ac-2
        given: confirmation prompt is shown
        when: user confirms (y/yes)
        then: operation proceeds
      - id: ac-3
        given: confirmation prompt is shown
        when: user declines (n/no)
        then: operation is cancelled with exit code 2
      - id: ac-4
        given: command is destructive
        when: --force flag is provided
        then: no confirmation prompt shown and operation proceeds
      - id: ac-5
        given: batch operation is destructive
        when: --refs provided without --force
        then: single confirmation covers all refs
      - id: ac-6
        given: command supports --force

    title: WebSocket Protocol Patterns

    acceptance_criteria:

        when: 30 seconds pass without activity
        then: server sends ping frame
      - id: ac-5
        given: ping was sent
        when: no pong received within 90 seconds
        then: connection is closed with code 1001
      - id: ac-6
        given: server sends events

        then: server pauses non-critical broadcasts until drain event
      - id: ac-7
        given: connection is closing

        given: client reconnects after disconnect
        when: new connection established

# PR #476 Review

## Findings

1. MUST-FIX (`src/cli/commands/session.ts:1166`)
The change replaces raw `console.log()` calls with `warn()` / `info()`, but those helpers intentionally suppress messages in structured modes (`--json`, `--yaml`). That fixes stdout JSON parsing, but it drops shadow sync/conflict diagnostics entirely instead of routing them to `stderr` as the linked task requires (`kspec task get @01KJ4SMC` explicitly says info/sync messages should go to stderr in `--json` mode).

2. SHOULD-FIX (`tests/cli/session-start-notes.test.ts:282`)
The new tests assert stdout JSON purity, but they do not exercise the sync-message branches (`syncResult.pulled` / `syncResult.hadConflict`) and do not assert `stderr`. As a result, they pass even when diagnostics are lost rather than redirected.

## AC / Spec Coverage Check

- PR body trailer found: `Task: @01KJ4SMC`
- `kspec task get @01KJ4SMC` references spec `@cmd-session-start` and notes trait `@trait-json-output`
- `kspec item get @cmd-session-start` currently reports no direct ACs and no inherited traits in this repo state
- `kspec item get @trait-json-output` shows trait ACs `ac-1`..`ac-6`
- The PR adds a `// AC: @trait-json-output ac-1` annotation, but the spec item itself does not currently declare/inherit that trait, so the task/spec/trait mapping is not encoded in spec metadata yet

## Validation / Tests Run

- `kspec validate` -> fails due pre-existing repo-wide issues (notably ambiguous `@observations` refs plus existing alignment/completeness warnings)
- `pnpm vitest run tests/cli/session-start-notes.test.ts` -> passed (12 tests)

MUST-FIX: `warn()`/`info()` are no-ops in structured modes (`output.ts` suppresses them when JSON/YAML is active). That keeps stdout parseable, but it also drops shadow sync/conflict diagnostics entirely. The linked task explicitly requires these messages to move to stderr in `--json` mode, so this does not satisfy the task intent. Please route these branches to stderr in structured mode instead of suppressing them.
SHOULD-FIX: These runtime assertions only prove stdout stays valid JSON. They never trigger a `syncResult.pulled` / `hadConflict` path and they do not assert stderr, so the current implementation can pass while silently dropping the sync diagnostics. Please add coverage for a sync-message case that asserts `stderr` contains the message and `stdout` remains pure JSON.
Remove this useless test. Real behavior tests only.

## Instructions

Run the task-work skill in loop mode:

```
/task-work loop
```

Loop mode means: no confirmations, auto-resolve decisions, automation-eligible tasks only.

**Normal flow:** Work on a task, create a PR, then stop responding. Ralph continues automatically —
it checks for remaining eligible tasks at the start of each iteration and exits the loop itself when none remain.

**Do NOT call `end-loop` after completing a task.** Simply stop responding.
`end-loop` is a rare escape hatch for when work is stalling across multiple iterations with no progress — not a normal exit path.

---
name: release
description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm.
---

# Release Skill

Create versioned releases with proper git tagging and GitHub release creation. The workflow is:

1. **Bump version** via PR (respects branch protection)
2. **Create tag** on the merged commit
3. **Create GitHub release** with notes
4. **CI publishes** to npm automatically

## When to Use

- After completing features/fixes ready for release
- When creating patch/minor/major version bumps
- For pre-release versions (alpha, beta, rc)
- When auditing what changes would be in a release (`--dry-run`)

**Prerequisites:**
- All related kspec tasks should be completed before release
- Run `npm test` locally to verify tests pass
- Ensure you're on `main` with a clean working tree

## Arguments

```
/release [patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z] [options]
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `patch` | Bug fixes, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.1.2) |
| `minor` | New features, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0) |
| `major` | Breaking changes (0.1.1 -> 1.0.0) |
| `X.Y.Z` | Explicit version number |
| (none) | Auto-detect from commits since last tag |

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Preview only - NO changes to git, tags, PRs, or GitHub |
| `--prerelease <type>` | Create prerelease (alpha, beta, rc) |

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Detect Context

Gather information about current state:

```bash
# Get current branch
git branch --show-current

# Check for uncommitted changes
git status --porcelain

# Get current version from package.json
node -p "require('./package.json').version"

# Get last tag
git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "no-tags"

# Get commits since last tag
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null)..HEAD --oneline
```

**Context to gather:**
- Current branch (must be `main`)
- Working tree status (must be clean)
- Current version in package.json
- Last tag (e.g., v0.1.1)
- Commits since last tag (count and list)

### Phase 2: Validate Constraints

All constraints must pass before proceeding:

| Constraint | Check | Error Message |
|------------|-------|---------------|
| On main branch | `git branch --show-current` = main | "Must be on main branch. Currently on: {branch}" |
| Clean working tree | `git status --porcelain` is empty | "Working tree must be clean. Commit or stash changes first." |
| Up to date with origin | After `git fetch`, local matches remote | "Local main is behind origin. Run: git pull" |
| Has releasable changes | At least one commit since last tag | "No changes since last tag {tag}. Nothing to release." |
| Tag doesn't exist | `git tag -l v{version}` is empty | "Tag v{version} already exists." |

**Dry-run behavior:** In dry-run mode, validation failures are reported but the preview continues. In normal mode, ANY validation failure stops execution immediately.

### Phase 3: Determine Version

If version type not specified, auto-detect from ALL commits since last tag:

```bash
# Get all commit messages since last tag (not just merges)
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%s%n%b"
```

**Auto-detection rules (conventional commits):**

| Pattern | Bump | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| `BREAKING CHANGE:` in body | major | Check commit body, not just subject |
| `feat!:` or `fix!:` (with `!`) | major | The `!` suffix indicates breaking |
| `feat:` or `feat(scope):` | minor | Scope is ignored for detection |
| `fix:`, `perf:`, `refactor:`, `chore:` | patch | Any maintenance work |

**Resolution order:**
1. If ANY commit has breaking change indicator -> major
2. Else if ANY commit starts with `feat:` -> minor
3. Else -> patch

**Prerelease handling (`--prerelease <type>`):**

| Current | Flag | Result | Rule |
|---------|------|--------|------|
| 0.1.1 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.0 | Bump patch, add prerelease |
| 0.1.2-alpha.0 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.1 | Same type: increment counter |
| 0.1.2-alpha.1 | `--prerelease beta` | 0.1.2-beta.0 | New type: reset counter to 0 |
| 0.1.2-rc.0 | (no flag) | 0.1.2 | Stable release: drop prerelease suffix |

**Prerelease rules:**
1. Same prerelease type -> increment counter (alpha.0 -> alpha.1)
2. Different prerelease type -> reset counter (alpha.1 -> beta.0)
3. No prerelease flag on prerelease version -> promote to stable

### Phase 4: Analyze Changes for Release Notes

Parse commits and categorize them for user-friendly release notes.

**Commit selection:**
- Prefer merge commits (contain `(#N)` PR reference) to avoid duplicates
- If no merge commits, include all commits matching conventional patterns
- Deduplicate by checking if a commit's changes are already in a merge commit

**Categorization (commit type -> section):**

| Commit Type | Release Notes Section |
|-------------|----------------------|
| `feat:` | Features & Additions |
| `fix:` | Bug Fixes |
| `perf:` | Performance |
| `refactor:`, `chore:`, `build:` | Other Changes |
| `test:`, `ci:`, `docs:` | (excluded unless user-facing) |

**kspec integration:**
```bash
# Extract completed task references from commit trailers
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%b" | grep -E "^Task: @" | sort -u
```

Completed tasks provide context for what was accomplished in this release.

### Phase 5: Preview (--dry-run)

For `--dry-run`, show comprehensive preview. **No changes are made** - no PRs, no tags, no releases.

```
## Release Preview (DRY RUN)

**Version bump:** 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (patch)
**Detection:** Auto-detected from 5 commits (3 fix, 2 chore)

### Validation
- [x] On main branch
- [x] Working tree clean
- [x] Up to date with origin
- [x] Has 5 commits since v0.1.1
- [x] Tag v0.1.2 does not exist

### Release Notes Preview

Bug fixes and improvements for kspec CLI.

#### Features & Additions
- Add JSON output mode for task list

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix author attribution for auto-generated notes
- Increase timeout for ref resolution

### Actions (dry-run: NOT executed)
1. Create version bump PR (package.json -> 0.1.2)
2. Wait for CI, then merge PR
3. Create tag: v0.1.2
4. Push tag to origin
5. Create GitHub release with notes above
6. CI will publish to npm

To execute: run `/release` without --dry-run
```

### Phase 6: Bump Version (PR)

**Before creating the tag**, update package.json via PR:

```bash
VERSION="0.1.2"  # calculated version

# Create branch for version bump
git checkout -b release/v$VERSION

# Update version without creating a tag
npm version $VERSION --no-git-tag-version

# Commit and push
git add package.json package-lock.json
git commit -m "chore: bump version to $VERSION"
git push -u origin release/v$VERSION

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "chore: bump version to $VERSION" --body "Prepare release v$VERSION"

# Wait for CI to pass, then merge
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
```

**Why version bump first?**
- The tagged commit has the correct version in package.json
- CI publishes exactly what's in package.json
- No out-of-sync state between git tag and package version

### Phase 7: Create Tag and Release

After the version PR is merged:

```bash
# Pull the merged version bump
git checkout main && git pull

# Create annotated tag (v prefix is convention for npm/semver)
git tag -a "v$VERSION" -m "Release v$VERSION"

# Push tag to origin
git push origin "v$VERSION"

# Create GitHub release (gh uses current repo automatically)
gh release create "v$VERSION" \
  --title "v$VERSION" \
  --notes "$(cat <<'EOF'
Brief summary of this release.

### Features & Additions
- Feature description

### Bug Fixes
- Fix description

### Other Changes
- Change description

**Full Changelog**: compare/v{previous}...v{version}
EOF
)"
```

**Tag naming:** Always use `v` prefix (e.g., `v0.1.2`) for consistency with npm versioning conventions and GitHub release detection.

**CI behavior:**
- Triggers on `release.published` event (within 1-2 minutes)
- Runs tests and publishes to npm with provenance
- Monitor progress at the repo's Actions tab

### Phase 8: Report Summary

After successful release:

```
## Release Complete

**Version:** v0.1.2
**Tag:** v0.1.2
**Commit:** abc1234

### Completed
- [x] Version PR created and merged
- [x] Tag created and pushed
- [x] GitHub release created
- [ ] CI publishing to npm... (check Actions tab)

**Release:** {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
**CI Status:** {repo}/actions
```

## Release Notes Format

Generate **friendly, user-facing release notes** (not raw commit dumps):

```markdown
Brief high-level summary of what this release brings (1-2 sentences).

### Features & Additions
- Feature description in plain language
- Another feature

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed issue with X when Y happened
- Resolved problem where Z

### Performance
- Improved speed of X operation

### Other Changes
- Updated internal handling of Y
- Refactored Z for maintainability

**Full Changelog**: {repo}/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2
```

**Writing guidelines:**
- Write in past tense ("Fixed", "Added", "Improved")
- Focus on user impact, not implementation details
- Group related changes together
- Omit test-only and CI-only changes
- Use repo-relative URLs (GitHub auto-links them)

## Error Handling

| Error | Recovery |
|-------|----------|
| Not on main | `git checkout main && git pull` |
| Dirty working tree | Commit or stash changes first |
| Behind origin | `git pull origin main` |
| No changes | Nothing to release since last tag |
| Tag exists | Choose different version or `git tag -d v{version}` then `git push origin --delete v{version}` |
| PR merge fails | Check CI status, fix issues, retry merge |
| `gh` not installed | Install GitHub CLI: https://cli.github.com/ |
| `gh` not authenticated | Run `gh auth login` |
| `gh` API rate limit | Wait and retry, or use `--limit` flag |

### Rollback Procedure

If something goes wrong after partial release:

**If tag was pushed but release failed:**
```bash
# Delete remote tag
git push origin --delete v$VERSION
# Delete local tag
git tag -d v$VERSION
# Fix issue and retry
```

**If release was created but CI publish failed:**
```bash
# Option 1: Delete and retry
gh release delete v$VERSION --yes
git push origin --delete v$VERSION
git tag -d v$VERSION
# Fix issue and retry from Phase 6

# Option 2: Manually trigger publish
# Go to Actions tab, run publish workflow manually
```

**If version PR was merged but you need to abort:**
```bash
# Revert the version bump
git revert HEAD
git push origin main
# The tag was never created, so nothing else to clean up
```

## Examples

### Standard patch release
```
User: /release patch
Agent: [Validates state]
Agent: [Creates version bump PR, waits for CI, merges]
Agent: [Creates v0.1.2 tag, pushes, creates GH release]

Release v0.1.2 created successfully.
- Version PR: #122 (merged)
- Tag: v0.1.2
- Release: {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
- CI publishing to npm...
```

### Auto-detect version
```
User: /release
Agent: [Analyzes 5 commits: 2 feat, 3 fix]
Detected: feat commits present -> minor bump (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0)
[Proceeds with release]
```

### Preview only
```
User: /release --dry-run
Agent: [Shows full preview, makes NO changes]
```

### Pre-release
```
User: /release minor --prerelease alpha
Agent: [Creates v0.2.0-alpha.0]
```

### Explicit version
```
User: /release 1.0.0

## Key Principles

- **Validation first**: Check all constraints before any changes
- **Dry-run is safe**: Preview makes zero changes
- **Friendly release notes**: Write for users, not developers
- **Branch protection compatible**: All changes via PR
- **CI handles publishing**: Skill creates release, CI publishes to npm
- **kspec integration**: Complete tasks before release, reference them in commits

## Troubleshooting

### npm Trusted Publishers OIDC Failures

If npm publish fails with "Access token expired or revoked" + 404:

**Root cause:** Older npm versions (10.8.x bundled with Node 18) have bugs with OIDC authentication for trusted publishers.

**Fix:** Ensure the publish workflow installs `npm@latest`:
```yaml

```

npm 11.x+ has the necessary fixes.

### PR Merge Blocked

If the version bump PR can't merge:

1. Check CI status - tests must pass
2. Check for merge conflicts - rebase if needed
3. Check branch protection rules - ensure you have merge permissions

### Tag Already Exists

If you need to re-release the same version:

```bash
# Delete existing tag (local and remote)
git tag -d v0.1.2
git push origin --delete v0.1.2

# Delete GitHub release if it exists
gh release delete v0.1.2 --yes

# Now retry the release
```

   142→| `perf:` | Performance |
   143→| `refactor:`, `chore:`, `build:` | Other Changes |
   144→| `test:`, `ci:`, `docs:` | (excluded unless user-facing) |
   145→
   146→**kspec integration:**
   147→```bash
   148→# Extract completed task references from commit trailers
   149→git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%b" | grep -E "^Task: @" | sort -u
   150→```
   151→
   152→Completed tasks provide context for what was accomplished in this release.
   153→
   154→### Phase 5: Preview (--dry-run)
   155→
   156→For `--dry-run`, show comprehensive preview. **No changes are made** - no PRs, no tags, no releases.
   157→
   158→```
   159→## Release Preview (DRY RUN)
   160→
   161→**Version bump:** 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (patch)
   162→**Detection:** Auto-detected from 5 commits (3 fix, 2 chore)
   163→
   164→### Validation
   165→- [x] On main branch
   166→- [x] Working tree clean
   167→- [x] Up to date with origin
   168→- [x] Has 5 commits since v0.1.1
   169→- [x] Tag v0.1.2 does not exist
   170→
   171→### Release Notes Preview
   172→
   173→Bug fixes and improvements for kspec CLI.
   174→
   175→#### Features & Additions
   176→- Add JSON output mode for task list
   177→
   178→#### Bug Fixes
   179→- Fix author attribution for auto-generated notes
   180→- Increase timeout for ref resolution
   181→
   182→### Actions (dry-run: NOT executed)
   183→1. Create version bump PR (package.json -> 0.1.2)
   184→2. Wait for CI, then merge PR
   185→3. Create tag: v0.1.2
   186→4. Push tag to origin
   187→5. Create GitHub release with notes above
   188→6. CI will publish to npm
   189→
   190→To execute: run `/release` without --dry-run
   191→```
   192→
   193→### Phase 6: Bump Version (PR)
   194→
   195→**Before creating the tag**, update package.json via PR:
   196→
   197→```bash
   198→VERSION="0.1.2"  # calculated version
   199→
   200→# Create branch for version bump
   201→git checkout -b release/v$VERSION
   202→
   203→# Update version without creating a tag
   204→npm version $VERSION --no-git-tag-version
   205→
   206→# Commit and push
   207→git add package.json package-lock.json
   208→git commit -m "chore: bump version to $VERSION"
   209→git push -u origin release/v$VERSION
   210→
   211→# Create PR
   212→gh pr create --title "chore: bump version to $VERSION" --body "Prepare release v$VERSION"
   213→
   214→# Wait for CI to pass, then merge
   215→gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
   216→```
   217→
   218→**Why version bump first?**
   219→- The tagged commit has the correct version in package.json
   220→- CI publishes exactly what's in package.json
   221→- No out-of-sync state between git tag and package version
   222→
   223→### Phase 7: Create Tag and Release
   224→
   225→After the version PR is merged:
   226→
   227→```bash
   228→# Pull the merged version bump
   229→git checkout main && git pull
   230→
   231→# Create annotated tag (v prefix is convention for npm/semver)
   232→git tag -a "v$VERSION" -m "Release v$VERSION"
   233→
   234→# Push tag to origin
   235→git push origin "v$VERSION"
   236→
   237→# Create GitHub release (gh uses current repo automatically)
   238→gh release create "v$VERSION" \
   239→  --title "v$VERSION" \
   240→  --notes "$(cat <<'EOF'
   241→Brief summary of this release.
   242→
   243→### Features & Additions
   244→- Feature description
   245→
   246→### Bug Fixes
   247→- Fix description
   248→
   249→### Other Changes
   250→- Change description
   251→
   252→**Full Changelog**: compare/v{previous}...v{version}
   253→EOF
   254→)"
   255→```
   256→
   257→**Tag naming:** Always use `v` prefix (e.g., `v0.1.2`) for consistency with npm versioning conventions and GitHub release detection.
   258→
   259→**CI behavior:**
   260→- Triggers on `release.published` event (within 1-2 minutes)
   261→- Runs tests and publishes to npm with provenance
   262→- Monitor progress at the repo's Actions tab
   263→
   264→### Phase 8: Report Summary
   265→
   266→After successful release:
   267→
   268→```
   269→## Release Complete
   270→
   271→**Version:** v0.1.2
   272→**Tag:** v0.1.2
   273→**Commit:** abc1234
   274→
   275→### Completed
   276→- [x] Version PR created and merged
   277→- [x] Tag created and pushed
   278→- [x] GitHub release created
   279→- [ ] CI publishing to npm... (check Actions tab)
   280→
   281→**Release:** {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
   282→**CI Status:** {repo}/actions
   283→```
   284→
   285→## Release Notes Format
   286→
   287→Generate **friendly, user-facing release notes** (not raw commit dumps):
   288→
   289→```markdown
   290→Brief high-level summary of what this release brings (1-2 sentences).
   291→
   292→### Features & Additions
   293→- Feature description in plain language
   294→- Another feature
   295→
   296→### Bug Fixes
   297→- Fixed issue with X when Y happened
   298→- Resolved problem where Z
   299→
   300→### Performance
   301→- Improved speed of X operation
   302→
   303→### Other Changes
   304→- Updated internal handling of Y
   305→- Refactored Z for maintainability
   306→
   307→**Full Changelog**: {repo}/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2
   308→```
   309→
   310→**Writing guidelines:**
   311→- Write in past tense ("Fixed", "Added", "Improved")
   312→- Focus on user impact, not implementation details
   313→- Group related changes together
   314→- Omit test-only and CI-only changes
   315→- Use repo-relative URLs (GitHub auto-links them)
   316→
   317→## Error Handling
   318→
   319→| Error | Recovery |
   320→|-------|----------|
   321→| Not on main | `git checkout main && git pull` |
   322→| Dirty working tree | Commit or stash changes first |
   323→| Behind origin | `git pull origin main` |
   324→| No changes | Nothing to release since last tag |
   325→| Tag exists | Choose different version or `git tag -d v{version}` then `git push origin --delete v{version}` |
   326→| PR merge fails | Check CI status, fix issues, retry merge |
   327→| `gh` not installed | Install GitHub CLI: https://cli.github.com/ |
   328→| `gh` not authenticated | Run `gh auth login` |
   329→| `gh` API rate limit | Wait and retry, or use `--limit` flag |
   330→
   331→### Rollback Procedure
   332→
   333→If something goes wrong after partial release:
   334→
   335→**If tag was pushed but release failed:**
   336→```bash
   337→# Delete remote tag
   338→git push origin --delete v$VERSION
   339→# Delete local tag
   340→git tag -d v$VERSION
   341→# Fix issue and retry
   342→```
   343→
   344→**If release was created but CI publish failed:**
   345→```bash
   346→# Option 1: Delete and retry
   347→gh release delete v$VERSION --yes
   348→git push origin --delete v$VERSION
   349→git tag -d v$VERSION
   350→# Fix issue and retry from Phase 6
   351→
   352→# Option 2: Manually trigger publish
   353→# Go to Actions tab, run publish workflow manually
   354→```
   355→
   356→**If version PR was merged but you need to abort:**
   357→```bash
   358→# Revert the version bump
   359→git revert HEAD
   360→git push origin main
   361→# The tag was never created, so nothing else to clean up
   362→```
   363→
   364→## Examples
   365→
   366→### Standard patch release
   367→```
   368→User: /release patch
   369→Agent: [Validates state]
   370→Agent: [Creates version bump PR, waits for CI, merges]
   371→Agent: [Creates v0.1.2 tag, pushes, creates GH release]
   372→
   373→Release v0.1.2 created successfully.
   374→- Version PR: #122 (merged)
   375→- Tag: v0.1.2
   376→- Release: {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
   377→- CI publishing to npm...
   378→```
   379→
   380→### Auto-detect version
   381→```
   382→User: /release
   383→Agent: [Analyzes 5 commits: 2 feat, 3 fix]
   384→Detected: feat commits present -> minor bump (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0)
   385→[Proceeds with release]
   386→```
   387→
   388→### Preview only
   389→```
   390→User: /release --dry-run
   391→Agent: [Shows full preview, makes NO changes]
   392→```
   393→
   394→### Pre-release
   395→```
   396→User: /release minor --prerelease alpha
   397→Agent: [Creates v0.2.0-alpha.0]
   398→```
   399→
   400→### Explicit version
   401→```
   402→User: /release 1.0.0
   403→Agent: [Creates v1.0.0 - useful for major milestones]
   404→```
   405→
   406→## Key Principles
   407→
   408→- **Version bump first**: PR before tag ensures package.json matches release
   409→- **Validation first**: Check all constraints before any changes
   410→- **Dry-run is safe**: Preview makes zero changes
   411→- **Friendly release notes**: Write for users, not developers
   412→- **Branch protection compatible**: All changes via PR
   413→- **CI handles publishing**: Skill creates release, CI publishes to npm
   414→- **kspec integration**: Complete tasks before release, reference them in commits
   415→
   416→## Troubleshooting
   417→
   418→### npm Trusted Publishers OIDC Failures
   419→
   420→If npm publish fails with "Access token expired or revoked" + 404:
   421→
   422→**Root cause:** Older npm versions (10.8.x bundled with Node 18) have bugs with OIDC authentication for trusted publishers.
   423→
   424→**Fix:** Ensure the publish workflow installs `npm@latest`:
   425→```yaml
   426→- name: Install latest npm
   427→  run: npm install -g npm@latest && npm --version
   428→```
   429→
   430→npm 11.x+ has the necessary fixes.
   431→
   432→### PR Merge Blocked
   433→
   434→If the version bump PR can't merge:
   435→
   436→1. Check CI status - tests must pass
   437→2. Check for merge conflicts - rebase if needed
   438→3. Check branch protection rules - ensure you have merge permissions
   439→
   440→### Tag Already Exists
   441→
   442→If you need to re-release the same version:
   443→
   444→```bash
   445→# Delete existing tag (local and remote)
   446→git tag -d v0.1.2
   447→git push origin --delete v0.1.2
   448→
   449→# Delete GitHub release if it exists
   450→gh release delete v0.1.2 --yes
   451→
   452→# Now retry the release
   453→```
   454→
   455→## Related Skills
   456→
   457→- `/pr` - Create pull requests (used internally by this skill)
   458→- `/audit` - Pre-release codebase review
   459→- `/kspec` - Task completion tracking
   460→
```

---
name: release
description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm.
---

# Release Skill

Create versioned releases with proper git tagging and GitHub release creation. The workflow is:

1. **Bump version** via PR (respects branch protection)
2. **Create tag** on the merged commit
3. **Create GitHub release** with notes
4. **CI publishes** to npm automatically

## When to Use

- After completing features/fixes ready for release
- When creating patch/minor/major version bumps
- For pre-release versions (alpha, beta, rc)
- When auditing what changes would be in a release (`--dry-run`)

**Prerequisites:**
- All related kspec tasks should be completed before release
- Run `npm test` locally to verify tests pass
- Ensure you're on `main` with a clean working tree

## Arguments

```
/release [patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z] [options]
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `patch` | Bug fixes, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.1.2) |
| `minor` | New features, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0) |
| `major` | Breaking changes (0.1.1 -> 1.0.0) |
| `X.Y.Z` | Explicit version number |
| (none) | Auto-detect from commits since last tag |

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Preview only - NO changes to git, tags, PRs, or GitHub |
| `--prerelease <type>` | Create prerelease (alpha, beta, rc) |

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Detect Context

Gather information about current state:

```bash
# Get current branch
git branch --show-current

# Check for uncommitted changes
git status --porcelain

# Get current version from package.json
node -p "require('./package.json').version"

# Get last tag
git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "no-tags"

# Get commits since last tag
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null)..HEAD --oneline
```

**Context to gather:**
- Current branch (must be `main`)
- Working tree status (must be clean)
- Current version in package.json
- Last tag (e.g., v0.1.1)
- Commits since last tag (count and list)

### Phase 2: Validate Constraints

All constraints must pass before proceeding:

| Constraint | Check | Error Message |
|------------|-------|---------------|
| On main branch | `git branch --show-current` = main | "Must be on main branch. Currently on: {branch}" |
| Clean working tree | `git status --porcelain` is empty | "Working tree must be clean. Commit or stash changes first." |
| Up to date with origin | After `git fetch`, local matches remote | "Local main is behind origin. Run: git pull" |
| Has releasable changes | At least one commit since last tag | "No changes since last tag {tag}. Nothing to release." |
| Tag doesn't exist | `git tag -l v{version}` is empty | "Tag v{version} already exists." |

**Dry-run behavior:** In dry-run mode, validation failures are reported but the preview continues. In normal mode, ANY validation failure stops execution immediately.

### Phase 3: Determine Version

If version type not specified, auto-detect from ALL commits since last tag:

```bash
# Get all commit messages since last tag (not just merges)
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%s%n%b"
```

**Auto-detection rules (conventional commits):**

| Pattern | Bump | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| `BREAKING CHANGE:` in body | major | Check commit body, not just subject |
| `feat!:` or `fix!:` (with `!`) | major | The `!` suffix indicates breaking |
| `feat:` or `feat(scope):` | minor | Scope is ignored for detection |
| `fix:`, `perf:`, `refactor:`, `chore:` | patch | Any maintenance work |

**Resolution order:**
1. If ANY commit has breaking change indicator -> major
2. Else if ANY commit starts with `feat:` -> minor
3. Else -> patch

**Prerelease handling (`--prerelease <type>`):**

| Current | Flag | Result | Rule |
|---------|------|--------|------|
| 0.1.1 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.0 | Bump patch, add prerelease |
| 0.1.2-alpha.0 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.1 | Same type: increment counter |
| 0.1.2-alpha.1 | `--prerelease beta` | 0.1.2-beta.0 | New type: reset counter to 0 |
| 0.1.2-rc.0 | (no flag) | 0.1.2 | Stable release: drop prerelease suffix |

**Prerelease rules:**
1. Same prerelease type -> increment counter (alpha.0 -> alpha.1)
2. Different prerelease type -> reset counter (alpha.1 -> beta.0)
3. No prerelease flag on prerelease version -> promote to stable

### Phase 4: Analyze Changes for Release Notes

Parse commits and categorize them for user-friendly release notes.

**Commit selection:**
- Prefer merge commits (contain `(#N)` PR reference) to avoid duplicates
- If no merge commits, include all commits matching conventional patterns
- Deduplicate by checking if a commit's changes are already in a merge commit

**Categorization (commit type -> section):**

| Commit Type | Release Notes Section |
|-------------|----------------------|
| `feat:` | Features & Additions |
| `fix:` | Bug Fixes |
| `perf:` | Performance |
| `refactor:`, `chore:`, `build:` | Other Changes |
| `test:`, `ci:`, `docs:` | (excluded unless user-facing) |

**kspec integration:**
```bash
# Extract completed task references from commit trailers
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%b" | grep -E "^Task: @" | sort -u
```

Completed tasks provide context for what was accomplished in this release.

### Phase 5: Preview (--dry-run)

For `--dry-run`, show comprehensive preview. **No changes are made** - no PRs, no tags, no releases.

```
## Release Preview (DRY RUN)

**Version bump:** 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (patch)
**Detection:** Auto-detected from 5 commits (3 fix, 2 chore)

### Validation
- [x] On main branch
- [x] Working tree clean
- [x] Up to date with origin
- [x] Has 5 commits since v0.1.1
- [x] Tag v0.1.2 does not exist

### Release Notes Preview

Bug fixes and improvements for kspec CLI.

#### Features & Additions
- Add JSON output mode for task list

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix author attribution for auto-generated notes
- Increase timeout for ref resolution

### Actions (dry-run: NOT executed)
1. Create version bump PR (package.json -> 0.1.2)
2. Wait for CI, then merge PR
3. Create tag: v0.1.2
4. Push tag to origin
5. Create GitHub release with notes above
6. CI will publish to npm

To execute: run `/release` without --dry-run
```

### Phase 6: Bump Version (PR)

**Before creating the tag**, update package.json via PR:

```bash
VERSION="0.1.2"  # calculated version

# Create branch for version bump
git checkout -b release/v$VERSION

# Update version without creating a tag
npm version $VERSION --no-git-tag-version

# Commit and push
git add package.json package-lock.json
git commit -m "chore: bump version to $VERSION"
git push -u origin release/v$VERSION

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "chore: bump version to $VERSION" --body "Prepare release v$VERSION"

# Wait for CI to pass, then merge
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
```

**Why version bump first?**
- The tagged commit has the correct version in package.json
- CI publishes exactly what's in package.json
- No out-of-sync state between git tag and package version

### Phase 7: Create Tag and Release

After the version PR is merged:

```bash
# Pull the merged version bump
git checkout main && git pull

# Create annotated tag (v prefix is convention for npm/semver)
git tag -a "v$VERSION" -m "Release v$VERSION"

# Push tag to origin
git push origin "v$VERSION"

# Create GitHub release (gh uses current repo automatically)
gh release create "v$VERSION" \
  --title "v$VERSION" \
  --notes "$(cat <<'EOF'
Brief summary of this release.

### Features & Additions
- Feature description

### Bug Fixes
- Fix description

### Other Changes
- Change description

**Full Changelog**: compare/v{previous}...v{version}
EOF
)"
```

**Tag naming:** Always use `v` prefix (e.g., `v0.1.2`) for consistency with npm versioning conventions and GitHub release detection.

**CI behavior:**
- Triggers on `release.published` event (within 1-2 minutes)
- Runs tests and publishes to npm with provenance
- Monitor progress at the repo's Actions tab

### Phase 8: Report Summary

After successful release:

```
## Release Complete

**Version:** v0.1.2
**Tag:** v0.1.2
**Commit:** abc1234

### Completed
- [x] Version PR created and merged
- [x] Tag created and pushed
- [x] GitHub release created
- [ ] CI publishing to npm... (check Actions tab)

**Release:** {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
**CI Status:** {repo}/actions
```

## Release Notes Format

Generate **friendly, user-facing release notes** (not raw commit dumps):

```markdown
Brief high-level summary of what this release brings (1-2 sentences).

### Features & Additions
- Feature description in plain language
- Another feature

### Bug Fixes

name: release
description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm.
---

# Release Skill

Create versioned releases with proper git tagging and GitHub release creation. The workflow is:

1. **Bump version** via PR (respects branch protection)
2. **Create tag** on the merged commit
3. **Create GitHub release** with notes
4. **CI publishes** to npm automatically

## When to Use

- After completing features/fixes ready for release
- When creating patch/minor/major version bumps
- For pre-release versions (alpha, beta, rc)
- When auditing what changes would be in a release (`--dry-run`)

**Prerequisites:**
- All related kspec tasks should be completed before release
- Run `npm test` locally to verify tests pass
- Ensure you're on `main` with a clean working tree

## Arguments

```
/release [patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z] [options]
```

| Argument | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `patch` | Bug fixes, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.1.2) |
| `minor` | New features, backwards-compatible (0.1.1 -> 0.2.0) |
| `major` | Breaking changes (0.1.1 -> 1.0.0) |
| `X.Y.Z` | Explicit version number |
| (none) | Auto-detect from commits since last tag |

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Preview only - NO changes to git, tags, PRs, or GitHub |
| `--prerelease <type>` | Create prerelease (alpha, beta, rc) |

## Workflow

### Phase 1: Detect Context

Gather information about current state:

```bash
# Get current branch
git branch --show-current

# Check for uncommitted changes
git status --porcelain

# Get current version from package.json
node -p "require('./package.json').version"

# Get last tag
git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null || echo "no-tags"

# Get commits since last tag
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0 2>/dev/null)..HEAD --oneline
```

**Context to gather:**
- Current branch (must be `main`)
- Working tree status (must be clean)
- Current version in package.json
- Last tag (e.g., v0.1.1)
- Commits since last tag (count and list)

### Phase 2: Validate Constraints

All constraints must pass before proceeding:

| Constraint | Check | Error Message |
|------------|-------|---------------|
| On main branch | `git branch --show-current` = main | "Must be on main branch. Currently on: {branch}" |
| Clean working tree | `git status --porcelain` is empty | "Working tree must be clean. Commit or stash changes first." |
| Up to date with origin | After `git fetch`, local matches remote | "Local main is behind origin. Run: git pull" |
| Has releasable changes | At least one commit since last tag | "No changes since last tag {tag}. Nothing to release." |
| Tag doesn't exist | `git tag -l v{version}` is empty | "Tag v{version} already exists." |

**Dry-run behavior:** In dry-run mode, validation failures are reported but the preview continues. In normal mode, ANY validation failure stops execution immediately.

### Phase 3: Determine Version

If version type not specified, auto-detect from ALL commits since last tag:

```bash
# Get all commit messages since last tag (not just merges)
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%s%n%b"
```

**Auto-detection rules (conventional commits):**

| Pattern | Bump | Notes |
|---------|------|-------|
| `BREAKING CHANGE:` in body | major | Check commit body, not just subject |
| `feat!:` or `fix!:` (with `!`) | major | The `!` suffix indicates breaking |
| `feat:` or `feat(scope):` | minor | Scope is ignored for detection |
| `fix:`, `perf:`, `refactor:`, `chore:` | patch | Any maintenance work |

**Resolution order:**
1. If ANY commit has breaking change indicator -> major
2. Else if ANY commit starts with `feat:` -> minor
3. Else -> patch

**Prerelease handling (`--prerelease <type>`):**

| Current | Flag | Result | Rule |
|---------|------|--------|------|
| 0.1.1 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.0 | Bump patch, add prerelease |
| 0.1.2-alpha.0 | `--prerelease alpha` | 0.1.2-alpha.1 | Same type: increment counter |
| 0.1.2-alpha.1 | `--prerelease beta` | 0.1.2-beta.0 | New type: reset counter to 0 |
| 0.1.2-rc.0 | (no flag) | 0.1.2 | Stable release: drop prerelease suffix |

**Prerelease rules:**
1. Same prerelease type -> increment counter (alpha.0 -> alpha.1)
2. Different prerelease type -> reset counter (alpha.1 -> beta.0)
3. No prerelease flag on prerelease version -> promote to stable

### Phase 4: Analyze Changes for Release Notes

Parse commits and categorize them for user-friendly release notes.

**Commit selection:**
- Prefer merge commits (contain `(#N)` PR reference) to avoid duplicates
- If no merge commits, include all commits matching conventional patterns
- Deduplicate by checking if a commit's changes are already in a merge commit

**Categorization (commit type -> section):**

| Commit Type | Release Notes Section |
|-------------|----------------------|
| `feat:` | Features & Additions |
| `fix:` | Bug Fixes |
| `perf:` | Performance |
| `refactor:`, `chore:`, `build:` | Other Changes |
| `test:`, `ci:`, `docs:` | (excluded unless user-facing) |

**kspec integration:**
```bash
# Extract completed task references from commit trailers
git log $(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD --pretty=format:"%b" | grep -E "^Task: @" | sort -u
```

Completed tasks provide context for what was accomplished in this release.

### Phase 5: Preview (--dry-run)

For `--dry-run`, show comprehensive preview. **No changes are made** - no PRs, no tags, no releases.

```
## Release Preview (DRY RUN)

**Version bump:** 0.1.1 -> 0.1.2 (patch)
**Detection:** Auto-detected from 5 commits (3 fix, 2 chore)

### Validation
- [x] On main branch
- [x] Working tree clean
- [x] Up to date with origin
- [x] Has 5 commits since v0.1.1
- [x] Tag v0.1.2 does not exist

### Release Notes Preview

Bug fixes and improvements for kspec CLI.

#### Features & Additions
- Add JSON output mode for task list

#### Bug Fixes
- Fix author attribution for auto-generated notes
- Increase timeout for ref resolution

### Actions (dry-run: NOT executed)
1. Create version bump PR (package.json -> 0.1.2)
2. Wait for CI, then merge PR
3. Create tag: v0.1.2
4. Push tag to origin
5. Create GitHub release with notes above
6. CI will publish to npm

To execute: run `/release` without --dry-run
```

### Phase 6: Bump Version (PR)

**Before creating the tag**, update package.json via PR:

```bash
VERSION="0.1.2"  # calculated version

# Create branch for version bump
git checkout -b release/v$VERSION

# Update version without creating a tag
npm version $VERSION --no-git-tag-version

# Regenerate kspec-agents.md so the version header stays in sync
kspec agents generate

# Commit and push
git add package.json package-lock.json kspec-agents.md
git commit -m "chore: bump version to $VERSION"
git push -u origin release/v$VERSION

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "chore: bump version to $VERSION" --body "Prepare release v$VERSION"

# Wait for CI to pass, then merge
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
```

**Why version bump first?**
- The tagged commit has the correct version in package.json
- CI publishes exactly what's in package.json
- No out-of-sync state between git tag and package version

### Phase 7: Create Tag and Release

After the version PR is merged:

```bash
# Pull the merged version bump
git checkout main && git pull

# Create annotated tag (v prefix is convention for npm/semver)
git tag -a "v$VERSION" -m "Release v$VERSION"

# Push tag to origin
git push origin "v$VERSION"

# Create GitHub release (gh uses current repo automatically)
gh release create "v$VERSION" \
  --title "v$VERSION" \
  --notes "$(cat <<'EOF'
Brief summary of this release.

### Features & Additions
- Feature description

### Bug Fixes
- Fix description

### Other Changes
- Change description

**Full Changelog**: compare/v{previous}...v{version}
EOF
)"
```

**Tag naming:** Always use `v` prefix (e.g., `v0.1.2`) for consistency with npm versioning conventions and GitHub release detection.

**CI behavior:**
- Triggers on `release.published` event (within 1-2 minutes)
- Runs tests and publishes to npm with provenance
- Monitor progress at the repo's Actions tab

### Phase 8: Report Summary

After successful release:

```
## Release Complete

**Version:** v0.1.2
**Tag:** v0.1.2
**Commit:** abc1234

### Completed
- [x] Version PR created and merged
- [x] Tag created and pushed
- [x] GitHub release created
- [ ] CI publishing to npm... (check Actions tab)

**Release:** {repo}/releases/tag/v0.1.2
**CI Status:** {repo}/actions
```

## Release Notes Format

Generate **friendly, user-facing release notes** (not raw commit dumps):

```markdown
Brief high-level summary of what this release brings (1-2 sentences).

### Features & Additions
- Feature description in plain language
- Another feature

### Bug Fixes
- Fixed issue with X when Y happened
- Resolved problem where Z

### Performance
- Improved speed of X operation

### Other Changes
- Updated internal handling of Y
- Refactored Z for maintainability

**Full Changelog**: {repo}/compare/v0.1.1...v0.1.2
```

**Writing guidelines:**
- Write in past tense ("Fixed", "Added", "Improved")
- Focus on user impact, not implementation details
- Group related changes together
- Omit test-only and CI-only changes
- Use repo-relative URLs (GitHub auto-links them)

## Error Handling

| Error | Recovery |
|-------|----------|
| Not on main | `git checkout main && git pull` |
| Dirty working tree | Commit or stash changes first |
| Behind origin | `git pull origin main` |
| No changes | Nothing to release since last tag |

| PR merge fails | Check CI status, fix issues, retry merge |
| `gh` not installed | Install GitHub CLI: https://cli.github.com/ |
| `gh` not authenticated | Run `gh auth login` |
| `gh` API rate limit | Wait and retry, or use `--limit` flag |

### Rollback Procedure

If something goes wrong after partial release:

**If tag was pushed but release failed:**
```bash

git push origin --delete v$VERSION
# Delete local tag
git tag -d v$VERSION
# Fix issue and retry
```

**If release was created but CI publish failed:**
```bash
# Option 1: Delete and retry
gh release delete v$VERSION --yes
git push origin --delete v$VERSION
git tag -d v$VERSION
# Fix issue and retry from Phase 6

# Option 2: Manually trigger publish
# Go to Actions tab, run publish workflow manually
```

```bash

git push origin main
# The tag was never created, so nothing else to clean up
```

- When auditing what changes would be in a release (`--dry-run`)

file.content:
# Create branch for version bump
git checkout -b release/v$VERSION

# Update version without creating a tag
npm version $VERSION --no-git-tag-version

# Regenerate kspec-agents.md so the version header stays in sync
kspec agents generate

# Commit and push
git add package.json package-lock.json kspec-agents.md
git commit -m "chore: bump version to $VERSION"
git push -u origin release/v$VERSION

# Create PR
gh pr create --title "chore: bump version to $VERSION" --body "Prepare release v$VERSION"

# Wait for CI to pass, then merge
gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch
```

**Why version bump first?**
- The tagged commit has the correct version in package.json
- CI publishes exactly what's in package.json
- No out-of-sync state between git tag and package version

**Why regenerate kspec-agents.md?**
- The freshness comment includes the kspec version (`Generated by kspec vX.Y.Z`)
- Regenerating after the version bump keeps the header in sync with the release
